items.title: Tasmanian wildlife department releases redacted thylacine witness statements dating back to 2001
items.who: DPIPWE (Tasmania)
items.note: First public release of the department's recent sighting file, with names, locations and photographs redacted.

items.title: James Cook University announces camera-trap search for thylacines on Cape York
items.who: S. Abell and W. Laurance (James Cook University)
items.note: Survey prompted by reported mainland sightings; no thylacine detections have been published from it.

items.title: Estimating the extinction date of the thylacine accounting for unconfirmed sightings
items.who: C. J. Carlson, A. L. Bond and K. R. Burgio
items.note: Preprint of the Bayesian mixed-certainty analysis that placed extinction most likely around 1940.

items.title: Genome of the Tasmanian tiger provides insights into the evolution and demography of an extinct marsupial carnivore
items.who: C. Y. Feigin et al.
items.note: Genome from a preserved museum pouch young showed low diversity and a long-term decline beginning well before human arrival.

items.title: High-quality fossil dates support a synchronous, Late Holocene extinction of devils and thylacines in mainland Australia
items.who: L. C. White, F. Saltré, C. J. A. Bradshaw and J. J. Austin
items.note: Radiocarbon dates place mainland extinction in the Late Holocene, the baseline against which claimed mainland sightings are judged.

items.title: Estimating the extinction date of the thylacine with mixed certainty data
items.who: C. J. Carlson, A. L. Bond and K. R. Burgio
items.note: Most likely extinction date 1940, with other estimators between 1936 and 1943 and none later than 1956.

items.title: Deficiencies in estimating the extinction date of the thylacine with mixed certainty data
items.who: B. W. Brook, S. R. Sleightholme, C. R. Campbell and J. C. Buettel
items.note: Argues that reporting biases make it premature to place extinction soon after the last captive animal died.

items.title: Reevaluating sighting models and moving beyond them to test and contextualize the extinction of the thylacine
items.who: C. J. Carlson, A. L. Bond and K. R. Burgio
items.note: Reply defending the original analysis and its conclusion that survival into recent decades is implausible.

items.title: The International Thylacine Specimen Database (6th Revision - Project Summary & Final Report)
items.who: S. R. Sleightholme and C. R. Campbell
items.note: Final report on the worldwide catalogue of surviving thylacine specimens, the reference list for any search for late-dated physical evidence.

items.title: A fast re-sampling method for using reliability ratings of sightings with extinction-date estimators
items.who: B. W. Brook, J. C. Buettel and I. Jarić
items.note: Re-sampling method and R script that let any extinction-date estimator use graded sightings, validated on species of known fate.

items.title: Right to Information release lists eight thylacine sightings reported to the department since 2016
items.who: DPIPWE (Tasmania)
items.note: Released reports from the Huon, Corinna, Waratah, Mt Roland and elsewhere; the department said none had been confirmed.

items.title: Footage of a Beaumaris Zoo thylacine from the 1935 travelogue Tasmania the Wonderland identified at the NFSA
items.who: B. Holmes, G. Linnard and M. Williams
items.venue: National Film and Sound Archive / Australian Geographic
items.note: Released as the latest known moving images of a living thylacine, filmed about 18 months before the last captive death.

items.title: A Catalogue of the Thylacine captured on film
items.who: S. R. Sleightholme and C. R. Campbell
items.note: Thylacine Image Registry of 112 known photographs with corrected provenance, the reference set for judging any new photographic claim.

items.title: The parson, the psychiatrist, the publican, and his nephews: the two final thylacine captures in Tasmania
items.who: G. Linnard, M. Williams and B. Holmes
items.venue: Papers and Proceedings of the THRA
items.note: Argues from council minutes and film evidence that the last captive thylacines were snared in the north-west around 1930.

items.title: Resolving when (and where) the Thylacine went extinct
items.who: B. W. Brook et al.
items.note: Preprint whose suggestion of possible survival into the late twentieth century drew wide press coverage two years before formal publication.

items.title: Resolving when (and where) the Thylacine went extinct
items.who: B. W. Brook, S. R. Sleightholme, C. R. Campbell, I. Jarić and J. C. Buettel
items.note: High-quality records imply extinction in the 1940s to 1970s; modelling all 1,237 records allows the late 1980s to early 2000s.

items.title: Thylacine: The History, Ecology and Loss of the Tasmanian Tiger
items.who: B. Holmes and G. Linnard (eds.)
items.note: Edited volume on the thylacine's history and ecology, including a chapter on the bounty years from 1830 to 1914.

items.title: The discovery of the remains of the last Tasmanian tiger (Thylacinus cynocephalus)
items.who: R. Paddle and K. Medlock
items.note: Identifies the skin and skeleton of the aged female that died on 7 September 1936 in the Tasmanian Museum's collection.

items.title: How collections and reputation were built out of Tasmanian violence: thylacines (Thylacinus cynocephalus) and Aboriginal remains from Morton Allport (1830–1878)
items.who: J. Ashby
items.note: Places the colonial trade in thylacine specimens alongside the trade in Aboriginal remains, shaping how museum records of the species should be read.

items.title: The Tasmanian Thylacine Sighting Record Database (TTSRD): 1,223 quality-rated and geo-located Thylacine observations from 1910 to 2019
items.who: B. W. Brook, S. R. Sleightholme, C. R. Campbell, I. Jarić and J. C. Buettel
items.note: Describes the deduplicated, dated, geo-tagged and quality-rated sighting database, each record linked to an image of its source.

items.title: Five previously undescribed thylacine (Thylacinus cynocephalus) specimens held in the museums of the University of Melbourne
items.who: R. Long
items.note: Describes five skulls accessioned between 1893 and 1932, showing that university teaching collections still hold uncatalogued specimens.

items.title: Inferring species extinction from sighting data
items.who: R. S. McCrea, T. Cheale, E. Campillo-Funollet and D. L. Roberts
items.note: Review of sighting-record extinction methods and their assumptions, with an RShiny application implementing several of them.

items.title: Illuminating the mystery of thylacine extinction: a role for relaxed selection and gene loss
items.who: B. G. Salve and N. Vijay
items.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
items.note: Identifies ancient gene losses in the thylacine genome and asks whether they increased vulnerability, bearing on causes rather than the date.
